title: Optimize quantized kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant & dequant fusion for lower latency
author: Rohit Mehra
description:
Context: quantized kernels for INT8/FP8 paths are a major latency and cost lever for production inference. SmoothQuant preprocessing (per-channel scaling) combined with dequantization fusion points had suboptimal microkernel scheduling and extra memory traffic, adding 10-25% tail latency on common Llama-family workloads. Motivation: reduce CPU/GPU kernel launch overhead, eliminate redundant dequant passes, and enable fused execution for common smoothquant + attention matmul patterns. This PR implements microkernel changes, a dequant fusion pass, and scheduler hints to improve continuous batching throughput without changing model outputs.

Summary of changes (single-string): implemented fused dequant+gemm kernels for INT8 and FP8 codepaths; added a smoothquant-aware lowering pass that emits fused ops when per-channel scales are stable; introduced a lightweight runtime hint (QuantFusionHint) so the request scheduler groups compatible requests for continuous batching; adjusted KV cache layout to reduce copies for fused execution; added unit and perf tests and updated docs and benchmark CI. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.

Approach and rationale: 1) Kernel: created quantized_fused_gemm_{int8,fp8}.cu that combines dequant->transpose->matmul in a single CUDA kernel for typical shapes (batch x seq x hidden where hidden % 64 == 0). Kernels accept per-channel scale vectors and apply smoothquant scaling internally to avoid temporary float buffers. 2) Fusion pass: new lowering pass runtime/ir/quant_fusion_pass.cpp inspects the graph for dequant->transpose->matmul patterns and rewrites them to fused_gemm ops when quant params are compile-time or stable at runtime. 3) Scheduler: continuous-batching scheduler updated to prefer grouping requests with identical quantization metadata (scale shapes and dtype) using QuantFusionHint; reduces kernel churn and improves batching efficiency. 4) KV cache: adjusted layout in runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache.cpp to support direct writes into kernel-friendly tiled memory to avoid the dequant->write->read sequence.

Benchmarks: microbench (Llama-2-7b, seq=2048, bs=1): baseline median latency 112ms -> optimized 96ms (-14%); p99 230ms -> 193ms (-16%). Throughput for continuous batching with mixed seq lengths improved by ~18% in our internal workload capture. Memory transient allocations reduced by ~40% on INT8 path. All perf numbers come from benchmarks/quant_int8_fp8.yaml run on p4d-equivalent hardware.

Compatibility and testing: outputs preserve FP32-equivalent behavior within expected quantization error (mean absolute diff < 1e-3 on eval prompts). Added tests in tests/quant/test_quant_fusion.py that validate numerical parity and in tests/perf/test_quant_bench.py for regression detection. CI includes a perf-check job that runs the microbenchmark and asserts non-regression threshold.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default; roll out to canary fleet for dedicated first, hosted next. Linear: ENG-2543 (kernel implementation) and ENG-2691 (scheduler + rollout). Jira: SUP-7421 for customer-reported tail-latency issue that motivated tuning. No breaking changes expected for API surface; internal ABI changes are guarded by runtime capability flags.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests
- [x] Fusion lowering pass + unit tests
- [x] Scheduler integration and end-to-end perf tests
- [x] KV cache layout adjustments
- [x] Documentation and release notes
- [x] Feature flag and gradual rollout plan

Notes: There was a transient CI flake on the first perf run due to driver mismatch; retriggered and CI green before merge. See review comments for small nit fixes applied.
